request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Admission Information:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Age: 54 years old
Gender: Male
Admission Date: [redacted]
Discharge Date: [redacted]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:

The patient was admitted to the hospital due to the dyspnea on exertion for more than 3 months. He had a history of cervical spondylosis, left side waist and leg pain for 20 years, and recurrent sinusitis and otitis media for 6 months. On physical examination, his vital signs were stable, and respiratory examination indicated decreased breath sounds in the bilateral lower hemithorax, with dullness on percussion. Laboratory results revealed the patient had anemia and elevated ESR, CA-125, and ADA levels. Analysis of the right side pleural fluid obtained by thoracentesis indicated an exudative type, and CT imaging of the chest showed bilateral pleural effusion, bilateral diffused pleural thickening, and multiple nodular lesions in the parietal pleura.

The patient was diagnosed with non-secretory multiple myeloma, and chemotherapy was initiated. After two rounds of chemotherapy, partial regression of pleural effusion, and pain relief were achieved. The patient was discharged and recommended for follow-up with the Department of Hematology. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications: None provided in the case report.

Discharge Instructions:
-The patient was recommended to follow-up with the Department of Hematology
-Continuation of recommended treatment
-Additional testing and consultations, as needed
-Recommended lifestyle modifications, as advised by the treating physician.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: C90**

The principal diagnosis is multiple myeloma (non-secretory), which the team established as the cause of the admission. It falls under category C90, plasma cell malignancies, in chapter C (malignant neoplasms). The pleural effusion and pleural involvement are manifestations of the myeloma and are not coded as the principal diagnosis.
